Everywhere you see, cloud solutions is sold as the next hottest thing in town.

However, I date back from a time where mainframes were being replaced by PC's. Freedom from the chains of permanent connection.

Then came the Thin Clients hype. Everything processed on a server and low cost PC's. (And failed)

Later you had the web-forms hype, everything as a HTML page, that would replace all modern software. (And failed)

Now this cloud hype. I predict that it is going to fail over the next few years. You can already see the cracks, Microsoft reducing the amount of cloud space you get. Those data-centers costs are more expensive than Microsoft claimed (energy, data transfers, aging hardware, aging power generators, aging batteries, increased operating costs and especially increased costs to fight off the hackers...)
The cloud hype. What do you think?

I can't wait for cloud to go away.

I avoid it for personal and work. I don't want all my data on a third party that might go belly up at the drop of a hat.

I've been unimpressed with the performance of cloud servers and the costs creep up on you. For the price, I'd rather just get a dedicated machine.

At work I have a rule my users can not use cloud services. If someone is using drop box for work under a personal account, and they quit/get hospitalized/etc, then we can't access their company files.

The scary part is that anything related to the cloud (including dropbox) wants to be your private data, and be your company data, and share anything with strangers like some social media.

The borderline between private, company and shared data is razor thin like a bit in the database. One small bit change, by a corrupt database entry and all your private and company data gets shared with the rest of the world. One idiot developer that forgot a "!" sign could expose your nude pictures to the company colleagues and your boss.

I also agree with you, there is no guarantee that Microsoft and Adobe can keep the operating costs under control and do not go belly up. Or worse, your company files being altered or wiped out because it is targeted by DMCA take down.

That's the thing exactly. When the data is on my servers I have control. I know if things are backed up and if that backup is valid. I have an easy recovery plan in case of failure. I know who has access.

Why pollute that?

And it cost exactly the same as the cloud.

No subscription fee, Not telecom fee, no support fee, instance fix when something breaks down, during a hack attack you pull the Internet plug. When a hacker locks you out from your admin account then you go to the server directly. Loss of Internet connectivity does not bring down your company.

And still with a cloud solution, you still need local servers to back up your data. And local servers to cache the database queries.

It is part of the big cycle. Same thing happens with physical data connection wires: Serial was all the rage (DB9 connectors, etc.) Then came along parallel cables. Now, we are back to serial (USB, SATA, etc.).

In a way, "cloud" computing is just a rehashing of mainframes and the cycle continues.

IMO the biggest problem with the cloud is that you are giving away your private data to private/unknown/far-away entities that you just can't trust.

Can anyone assure me that the data i put on Dropbox will still be there in 20 years? What if Dropbox goes bankrupt? Look at Geocities for example... thousands of persons trusted them with their personal websites, many of those websites were pretty much the only "online heritage" left by people that is not anymore among us... then Yahoo bought them and shut them off because Geocities didn't make them enough of a profit. All the informations stored in Geocities are effectively lost, including pictures, technical data, thoughts, etc. And i should give my pictures, my most personal data, my thoughts, my stuff to someone that can just delete it all tomorrow?

Beside this there is the big problem of governments that keep thinking that online you have no rights at all. Even if you happen to trust Microsoft/Dropbox/Box/... they will HAVE to surrender your data if the government asks for it. Until these two points are addressed there is no way i'll use the cloud for more than file sharing and for storing data with little or no value to me.
